summary: Charon is a "Google Maps for Mars" built for astronauts on foot. It starts as an interactive 3D globe of Mars and turns into a detailed 2D surface map as you zoom in. Pick a destination and Charon finds the route that uses the least oxygen, based on terrain slope, elevation and distance. It gives step by step instructions and tells you in real time whether you have enough oxygen to make it back to your homebase.
details:
Charon works like a navigation app with oxygen as the main limit.
How it works: a 3D globe switches to a 2D map as you zoom. A pathfinding algorithm weights each step by slope, elevation change and distance to estimate oxygen use. It then picks the safest, most efficient route and compares the return-trip cost with the oxygen left.
Features: routes optimized for oxygen, turn-by-turn instructions, a "can I make it back?" indicator and a 3D ground-level terrain preview.
Impact: helps mission planners and astronauts lower risk during EVAs and plan surface exploration more safely.
Tools: [e.g. JavaScript, Three.js / CesiumJS, HTML/CSS].
Creativity: most Mars maps only show the surface. Charon makes the map an active survival tool, with route planning by life-support budget and an immersive 3D preview.
